subject: Cross-region Reserved Pools — pricing structure & replication/DR options
messages:
From: Laurie Chen <laurie.chen@auroraai.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Aurora AI Procurement <procurement@auroraai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Need multi-region committed pricing for Dedicated capacity

Hi Dev,

Thanks for the product tour last week — the Dedicated capacity demo was helpful. Aurora is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a low-latency inference tier for our customer-facing features. Two quick asks so our procurement and infra teams can model costs: 

1) A committed (12/24 mo) reserved pricing grid for separate GPU pools in US and EU (we want independent pools per region, not a single global pool).
2) Clarification on the cost and options for cross-region replication / warm-standby (we need RTO < 5m for regional failover).
3) What throughput guarantees (tokens/sec per GPU) you commit to, and how those change with batching / quantization.

Can you also sketch any discount tiers tied to committed vGPU-hours or multi-region commits? We expect a blended monthly token volume around 2B tokens across both regions initially.

Appreciate a short proposal and ballpark numbers by next Wed (17 Feb) so procurement can prepare.

—Laurie
Laurie Chen
Head of Infrastructure
Aurora AI

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Laurie Chen <laurie.chen@auroraai.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Need multi-region committed pricing for Dedicated capacity

Laurie —

Thanks — I put together an initial approach and attached a short pricing sheet (RI_Dedicated_Pricing_v3.pdf). High level:

- Architecture: Independent reserved GPU pools per region (US West + EU West). Each pool is reserved capacity (vGPU-hour based commit) with optional cross-region warm-standby replication.
- Pricing model: Base rate per vGPU-hour per region, with discount bands based on committed vGPU-hours per month and an additional 10% cross-region multi-pool discount when you commit to both regions on a single contract.
- DR/replication: Warm-standby (replicated model weights + KV cache warmers) is priced as a 'replication footprint' percentage (typically 25–40% of the primary pool cost). For RTO < 5m we recommend a minimal hot standby (50% of primary capacity) in the failover region.
- Throughput: We guarantee 95th percentile latency SLOs; throughput per vGPU varies by model and sequence length. Ballpark: for 8k-context Llama-Style medium models, expect ~60–80 tokens/sec per A100-80GB vGPU baseline; quantized/fp16 variants increase throughput by ~1.3x–1.8x in practice. We include continuous batching and KV caching optimizations.

I flagged a few pricing levers in the sheet: commit length (12 vs 24), vGPU sizing (A100 vs H100 equivalents), and cross-region discount. If this looks reasonable I can translate to a draft SOW and contract language.

Attaching pricing PDF. I'll follow up with a tailored example for your estimated 2B tokens/month (calls out required vGPU-hours and a recommended commit).

Best,
Dev Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Aurora pricing — verify replication math and discount bands

Looping you both in — Laurie asked for specific numbers for Aurora's 2B token estimate. Two items I want us aligned on before we send the detailed SOW:

- Replication pricing: Dev suggested 25–40% of primary for warm-standby, but for RTO <5m we should outline a 50% hot-standby option clearly priced and call out costs for replication bandwidth during syncs.
- Discounting: Instead of a flat 10% multi-region add-on, propose tiered discounts: 5% (>=3k vGPU-hrs/mo), 10% (>=8k), 15% (>=20k) and an extra 5% for dual-region contract on 24-mo commits. That preserves margin while giving procurement something to work with.

Also confirm the throughput numbers you used to convert 2B tokens into vGPU-hours and whether we recommend mixed GPU profile (H100 in US, A100 or H100-small in EU) to optimize costs.

On region pricing: EU tends to be 8–12% higher (energy/regulatory), so include region multipliers.

—Marissa
VP, Sales Engineering

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aurora pricing — verify replication math and discount bands

Quick calc notes (keeping it brief):

- Assumption: avg response length 150 tokens, average prompt+response per request ~300 tokens. 2B tokens / 300 = ~6.7M requests/mo.
- Baseline throughput: H100 ~120 tokens/s (8k context, small-medium models); A100 ~70 tokens/s. Use a blended vGPU mix: US (H100-heavy) for latency-critical, EU (A100 or H100-small) for cost efficiency.
- vGPU-hours estimate: assume effective tokens/sec util after batching ~0.65 of theoretical; for 2B tokens that's ~9.5k vGPU-hours/month (blended).
- Replication: Hot-standby (50%) adds ~50% additional vGPU-hours billed at standby rate; warm-standby (25%) adds ~25%. The replication footprint percent Dev used looks okay but call out network egress during sync windows.

I'll drop a concise table in the SOW showing three SKU examples: 1) US-only 24-mo commit, 2) US+EU 12-mo dual commit (warm-standby), 3) US+EU 24-mo (hot-standby + multi-region discount).

—Alex
Principal Solutions Architect

Subject: Cross-region Reserved Pools — pricing structure & replication/DR options

Laurie —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a short SOW and three pricing scenarios tailored to Aurora's 2B token estimate:

Scenario A — US primary (24-mo commit)
- Blended 7x H100 equivalent vGPUs (latency optimized).
- Committed vGPU-hours: 9,000/mo.
- Effective list rate: $X per vGPU-hour (region multiplier applied).
- Discount: 12% (24-mo tier)
- No replication (single region).

Scenario B — US + EU (12-mo commits, warm-standby)
- US primary + EU warm-standby (25% replication footprint).
- Committed vGPU-hours: US 6,500/mo, EU 2,500/mo standby.
- Multi-region discount: 10% across combined commit.
- Recommended: include a 2-week failover test twice/year.

Scenario C — US + EU (24-mo commits, hot-standby for <5m RTO)
- Hot-standby sized at 50% of primary in failover region (always warm/ready).
- Committed vGPU-hours charged for both regions; replication premium applied.
- Total discount: 15% + 5% dual-region add-on (20% effective at scale).

Notes:
- Throughput guarantees: 95th pct latency SLOs in SOW. Token/sec numbers are included per SKU and will be verified during onboarding.
- Pricing details, lines for KMS integration and network egress, and termination/upgrade clauses are in the attached SOW draft (SOW_Draft_Aurora.docx).

If this aligns with your procurement needs, we can: 1) lock the scenario and draft order form, 2) schedule legal/ops review, and 3) set a migration/onboarding kickoff.

Would you like an itemized vGPU-hour-to-token mapping for each scenario? Happy to supply that in the next note.

Best regards,
